title: Bringing Balinese Manuscripts to Wikimania 2026
content:
At Wikimania 2026 in Paris, Carma Citrawati and I presented “From Wikilontar to Wikisami: How Regional Partnerships Power Community-Led Growth in Bali.” The session explored how a local initiative to preserve Balinese manuscripts gradually developed into a regional learning program and, later, engagement with international memory institutions.

Carma opened the session by introducing the audience to lontar, traditional Balinese manuscripts containing knowledge about history, literature, spirituality, medicine, and everyday life. Many of these manuscripts are fragile, difficult to access, or held in collections outside Bali.

To make the story more tangible, Carma brought a copy of a lontar manuscript from Bali, written on palm leaves. Seeing the manuscript in person helped the audience understand that this work is not only about digitizing old documents. It is also about reconnecting communities with living knowledge passed down through generations.

title: “Don’t Blink”: Protecting the Wikimedia model, its people, and its values in July 2026
content:
Welcome to “Don’t Blink”! Every month we share public policy developments from around the world that shape people’s ability to participate in the free knowledge movement. In case you blinked last month, here are the most important advocacy topics that have kept the Wikimedia Foundation busy.

The Global Advocacy team works to advocate laws and government policies that protect the volunteer community-led Wikimedia model, Wikimedia’s people, and the Wikimedia movement’s core values. To learn more about us and the work we do with the rest of the Foundation: follow us on LinkedIn, X (formerly Twitter), and Bluesky; sign up for our quarterly newsletter or Wikimedia public policy mailing list; and visit our Meta-Wiki webpage.

title: Partnerships, People, and Possibilities: The Content Partnerships Hub at Wikimania
content:
Wikimania 2026 brought the Wikimedia movement together in Paris this summer, and the Content Partnerships Hub (CPH) was there in full force. It was a fantastic opportunity for us not only to speak to the whole Wikimedia movement about our achievements and activities, but also to spend time together and have valuable discussions about the future of our project in person. Spread across several countries and time zones, from Chile to Sweden, we do not get this opportunity often!

Over the course of the conference, CPH members ran a number of sessions focusing on different aspects of our work as well as a physical helpdesk. They were all well-attended and we were excited to hear your thought-provoking questions and input. In this post, we re-cap what we did – if you find it interesting, make sure to look at the recordings.

title: Wikimedia Community User Group Uganda: Powering Open Knowledge Through Strategic Partnerships
content:
At Wikimedia Community User Group Uganda (WCUGU), we believe free knowledge thrives when communities, institutions, and innovators work together. Formal partnerships, sealed through signed Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs), allow us to scale impact, build sustainable programmes, and ensure Ugandan voices, languages, culture, and heritage are better represented on Wikipedia, Wikidata, Wikimedia Commons, and related platforms.

In recent months we have formalized three particularly exciting collaborations: with the Community Libraries Association of Uganda (COLAU), Sunbird AI, Uganda Premier League (UPL) and Kabale University. Each partnership strengthens a different pillar of our work libraries and GLAM, language technology, and higher education while advancing our shared commitment to inclusive, locally relevant open knowledge.

Libraries are vital gateways to information, education, and community development. Our partnership with COLAU, formalized through a signed MoU, focuses on expanding access to knowledge and documenting Uganda’s cultural and educational resources under the GLAM-Wiki banner.

title: What’s next for Capacity Exchange? A new cycle of outreach, feedback, and (tech) collaboration
content:
After three years of development, Capacity Exchange (CapX) has entered a new cycle. Funded through a Wikimedia CH grant, from July to December 2026, we will be working to bring the tool to communities around the world and gather feedback from users, with a particular focus on community managers and leaders.

In this cycle, we are focused on building relationships with community managers and leaders, introducing them to CapX and exploring how it can help them carry out their work more easily and with better data to inform their decisions. We also want to understand how the tool could be improved for this audience and explore ways of adapting it to their needs.

Finally, we are presenting the possibilities of working with the CapX API to develop tools and solutions tailored to specific community needs.

Read more about these activities below.

This new cycle is focused on outreach, community engagement, and understanding how CapX can be useful in the everyday work of Wikimedia communities.

title: Kambari Wikipedia Outreach
content:
From Tsuvadi to Shingini: Building a Wikimedia Community for the Kambari Language in Nigeria

What began as an outreach project focused on the Tsuvadi language grew into a broader initiative to introduce Wikimedia projects to speakers of the Kambari language and lay the foundation for a sustainable Kambari Wikimedia community.

The project was initially designed around Tsuvadi, but consultations with the Language Development Translation and Initiative (LDTI), traditional leaders, and community members revealed that Tsuvadi is one of the varieties of the broader Shingini (Kambari) language. Based on these consultations, the project was expanded to include three major varieties: Tsishingini, spoken in the Salka area; Cishingini, spoken in the Agwara area; and Tsikimba, spoken in the Auna area.

This change made the project more representative of the Kambari-speaking community and provided contributors with the opportunity to work in the variety they were most familiar with.
snippet: From Tsuvadi to Shingini: Building a Wikimedia Community for the Kambari Language in Nigeria
creator: Danjuma Anthony

title: Free Photography Has No License to Be Bad
content:
Every August 19, the world celebrates the camera as a tool of connection — and for the free knowledge movement, it’s also a reminder of what a single photograph can unlock. On Wikimedia Commons, a well-lit image of a market stall, a sacred hill, or a rare frog isn’t just decoration. It’s the visual backbone that lets millions of Wikipedia readers actually see the subject they came to learn about.

There’s a persistent myth that free-licensed photography is a compromise, that the “good” images live behind stock-photo paywalls, and Commons gets the leftovers. Our community’s work says otherwise. Across campaigns like Wiki Loves Africa, Wiki Loves Earth, and Wiki Loves Monuments, Malagasy wikimedia contributors have uploaded more than 7,000 photographs to Wikimedia Commons; many shot with the same care, composition, and technical rigor as a commissioned assignment. Free licensing describes who can use an image, not how well it was made.

title: Strengthening Kinyarwanda Through Mentorship & Community
content:
Wikimedia Kinyarwanda Community Hub (Wikipedia Kinyarwanda): A Wikimedia language community in Rwanda (Africa). The main focus is to build a sustainable community, increasing free content in Kinyarwanda on open Wikimedia projects in Rwanda.

Mentorship program focuses on overcoming specific technical, organizational, and outreach barriers to sustainable growth. This was a good program for Kinyarwanda language, we had a significant participation, a lot of contributions on Kinyarwanda Wikipedia. Number of articles has been increased and article quality has been improved.

The LDH mentorship program was very important for the whole community. We appreciated the time our mentors ( John & Tochi) took to train us , to teach us new things, and to gain technical knowledge about language diversity. The mentorship also helped better understand how to develop sustainable activities, engage the Kinyarwanda community, and create meaningful impact for the Kinyarwanda language. 

Recruit and train new editors : This goal has been well achieved, currently we have new active editors 42.4% new Wikimedians recruited, 15.2 % are trained from scratch and they are contributing without any issue.

title: Wikimania 2026 Tandem Scholarship by Wikimedia Deutschland Report
content:
I’m a volunteer with the Wikimedia Tanzania community, contributing to Wikimedia Commons, Lingua Libre, Wikidata, and Swahili Wikipedia. I also work as a Program Coordinator for the Digital Youth Clubs Program in Tanzania. I attended Wikimania 2026 in Paris on a Tandem Scholarship funded by Wikimedia Deutschland, and here is a report of my experience.

A pre-conference for women across Wikimedia communities. One of the things I gained from the pre-conference was discovering the Wiki Women Conference. I had never known that such a conference existed within the Wikimedia movement. It was inspiring to see a dedicated space where women could openly share experiences, and encourage one another to take on leadership roles and contribute to closing gender gaps across Wikimedia projects.

The summit continued after lunch on gender equity, I learned about the #VisibleWikiWomen campaign which inspired to give women the visibility and acknowledgement they deserve by uploading quality images to Wikimedia commons.

title: Achieving 100,000 Entries: A Milestone Journey for Swahili Wiktionary
content:
On August 16, 2025, our community gathered at the SeedSpace hall on the 7th floor of Tanzanite Park, Victoria. True to the venue’s name, that day marked the planting of a crucial seed: a collective effort to revitalize and expand the Swahili Wiktionary.

On that unforgettable day for the Wikimedia movement in Tanzania, the Jenga Wikipedia ya Kiswahili affiliate community committed to an ambitious target: to reach 100,000 entries by August 16, 2026. At the launch of this vision, the Wiktionary statistics banner stood at just 15,926 entries. Through targeted campaign efforts alone, our contributors generated over 11,300 entries—a testament to absolute dedication and a shared resolve to advance open knowledge in Swahili. View full report on Meta: Jenga Wikipedia ya Kiswahili/Report 2025— 2026 – Meta-Wiki

Our initial strategy relied on a structured rotation across Wikimedia platforms—dedicating one month to Wikipedia and the next to Wiktionary. We sustained this momentum from June 2025 through April 11, 2026, when we officially joined forces with the Wikimedians of Arusha Community User Group.

title: Language and Internationalization/Newsletters/11
content:
Welcome to the July 2026 edition of the Language and internationalization newsletter by the Wikimedia Foundation Wikimedia Language and Product Localization team! This newsletter provides you with quarterly updates on new feature developments, improvements in various language-related technical projects and support work, community meetings, and ideas to get involved in contributing to the projects.

Subscribe to the newsletter

translatewiki.net is a platform for gathering translations of interface messages for Wikipedia and its sister projects. This quarter, 7 new projects, including a MediaWiki Extension Recent Activity and Wikivoyage Listing Editor, were added to the platform. In addition, Lakota (lkt), an endangered Native American language with fewer than 10,000 speakers, was added to MediaWiki [1]. Two volunteers also made improvements to language support, including updates to magic word configuration for Karakalpak [2] and localization of MediaWiki language messages for Pashto [3].
